# What patients tell the front desk

The front desk clerk keeps an informal notebook of things patients say when they cancel or fail to return, because nobody ever asked her to but she noticed the answers kept rhyming with each other. The most common thing patients say, in one phrasing or another, is some version of "I didn't think I still needed to come." The second most common is a version of "I wasn't sure the follow-up would be different from the first visit."

Read together, those two answers are not really about transport or money, though both come up too; they are about whether the patient understands what the second visit is actually for. Nobody on staff has ever asked a patient directly, "what do you think happens at the follow-up visit that didn't already happen at the first one." The clerk's notebook is the closest thing the clinic has to that question being asked at all, and it was never designed as data, it was just one person paying attention long enough to notice a pattern repeating.
